sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax on a Victoria home?
sections.html:
Three separate offices touch a Victoria bill. The Victoria Central Appraisal District values the property, each taxing unit picks its own rate, and the Victoria County Tax Office mails the statement and takes the money.

The Census Bureau counts Victoria at 66,500 people for mid-2025, a gain of 1.5% since 2020, on roughly 37 square miles. In the 2020 to 2024 survey, owners occupy 57.9% of homes, the median home is valued at $207,100 and median rent is $1,172. Those numbers explain why homestead rules matter here: most bills are on modest homes, so a fixed-dollar school exemption removes a large share of the school value.

The appraisal district's own page lists who does what. It determines values, mails notices of appraised value, handles protests and administers exemptions. The taxing entities set budgets and rates. The tax assessor-collector calculates and distributes bills and collects payment. Inside city limits, one bill can carry county, school, city and sometimes junior college, hospital or road district charges.

  • Value, exemptions, name and address changes: Victoria Central Appraisal District, 2805 N. Navarro St., Suite 300, phone (361) 576-3621, weekdays 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
  • Bills, payments, penalty questions: the Victoria County Tax Office, 205 N. Bridge St., Suite 101, phone (361) 576-3671.
  • City rate and budget questions: the City of Victoria.

sections.h2: What is the Victoria city tax rate?
sections.html:
The city's 2025 rate was $0.4790 per $100 of taxable value, and the city's 2026 meeting notice proposed $0.4538. A city notice posted on September 9, 2026 says the council adopted a rate. The figure on your own statement is the final word.

The city's meeting notice also sets out the voter-approval and no-new-revenue rates. It lists $0.4538 as the no-new-revenue rate and $0.4652 as the voter-approval rate for 2026. Those two benchmarks bracket the council's choice.

sections.h2: What deadlines and late charges apply to a Victoria bill?
sections.html:
The county tax office mails statements in October, and payment is owed on receipt. Nothing is late before February 1, so January 31 is the practical deadline.

The county's explanation: the penalty opens at 6%, climbs a point on the first of each later month, then adds 2 points on July 1 to reach 12%. Interest is separate, at 1% for each month. A payment mailed late in January counts only if the post office postmarks the envelope by January 31. The Comptroller notes that units with collection attorneys may add up to 20 percent more on accounts still open in July.

The county tax office receives the certified roll from the appraisal district by July 25, then combines it with each unit's adopted rate to produce the October statements. The district's calendar lists mid-April for appraisal notices and August to September for rate setting.

  • If no statement arrives by November 1, ask the tax office to mail one. A bill that never arrived does not excuse the tax or release the lien.
  • With an escrow account, put your loan number on any statement that reaches you and forward it to the lender.
  • Lenders have to ask the county for their clients' statements by late August, or the owner may get the bill directly.

sections.h2: How can a Victoria homeowner lower the property tax bill?
sections.html:
File a residence homestead exemption with the appraisal district, and protest the value if the notice looks too high. Both steps happen at the appraisal district, not at the tax office.

A home qualifies for the general exemption when it is the owner's main residence on January 1. Homeowners at 65 and up get an additional exemption, and there are separate exemptions for disabled homeowners and for disabled veterans and their surviving spouses. School districts statewide give a $140,000 homestead exemption, plus $60,000 more to seniors and disabled owners. A taxing unit may also adopt a percentage exemption of its own, so ask which local options apply to Victoria units.

Victoria CAD's exemption page lists what an applicant must supply under House Bill 585:

  • A copy of a Texas driver license or Texas ID card, with the property address matching the address on the license, vehicle registration or a utility bill.
  • A statement that no other homestead is claimed in or outside Texas.
  • Manufactured homes need a statement of ownership and location from the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs.

Active duty military members and their spouses can ask the chief appraiser to waive the address match. The exemption is not an annual application unless the chief appraiser asks you to reapply. Forms are on the district's Forms page, and the district takes completed exemption forms at exemptions@victoriacad.org.

Homesteads also have a state cap of 10% a year on appraised value growth once the first qualifying year has passed. A school tax freeze for seniors and disabled owners can follow them to a replacement Texas homestead.

sections.h2: How do I protest my Victoria appraisal?
sections.html:
Get a notice of protest to the appraisal district by May 15, or by the 30th day after your appraisal notice arrives when that date falls later. The district's taxpayer page links Form 50-132, a guide to filling it out, and the Comptroller's video on presenting a case.

The calendar on that page lists mid-April for the mailing of notices and May 15 for the protest deadline. The district accepts protests at protest@victoriacad.org. If the review board's order still looks wrong, the Comptroller lists court, binding arbitration or the State Office of Administrative Hearings as next steps.

sections.h2: How can I pay Victoria County property tax?
sections.html:
You can pay in person at a county tax office, by mail, by phone or online. Partial payments are accepted, though any balance left after January 31 starts to collect penalty and interest.

  • In person: cash, check, money order, debit or credit card. A convenience fee applies to cards.
  • By phone at 877-253-4085, for Victoria County accounts only. The county lists a 2.30% card fee with a $1 minimum and a flat $0.50 fee for an electronic check.
  • By mail: write the account number and the words "partial payment" on a partial payment.
  • A returned check carries a $30 service charge.

Seniors and disabled homeowners can ask about the four-installment option.

sections.h2: How does a sale change who pays the Victoria tax?
sections.html:
The lien securing each year's tax arrives on January 1 and stays with the house, which is why closing agents pay the year's tax from the seller's funds. The county tax office tells new buyers to check their closing papers, because the title company may have collected from the seller and credited the buyer.

Whoever owned on January 1 stays liable for that year's tax after a sale. Delinquent tax blocks clear title, so a late Victoria account gets paid off from the proceeds. Before listing, get a balance for every unit from the tax office.

A buyer who closes mid-year may qualify for the exemption on the rest of that tax year when the seller never held it.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 Victoria city tax rate adopted?
faqs.a: The City of Victoria posted a notice on September 9, 2026 that it adopted a 2026 rate. The city's meeting notice proposed $0.4538 per $100, so confirm the final figure on your statement or with the tax office at (361) 576-3671.

faqs.q: When does Victoria property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1. A payment postmarked by January 31 counts as on time. After that the county starts the 6% penalty and 1% interest, and the penalty keeps growing each month until it tops out at 12% on July 1.

faqs.q: Which Victoria office changes my value or exemption?
faqs.a: The Victoria Central Appraisal District, reachable at (361) 576-3621. The county tax office sends bills but says the appraisal district makes every change to values, exemptions and account details.

faqs.q: Can I pay only part of my Victoria tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The county tax office takes partial payments, but whatever remains after January 31 starts to accrue penalty and interest. Put the account number and the words partial payment on the check.

faqs.q: Does a Victoria buyer owe the seller's unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Unpaid tax stays with the house until it is cleared. The county tells new owners to read their closing papers to see who paid.
